messages:
Sam K: Quick sync — noticed an uptick in perceived latency for token streaming after the recent kernel selection tweak. p95 for stream-first-byte is up ~30ms on our low-latency tier. Anyone else seeing this?
Yara M: Saw it in dashboards this morning. Throughput steady but tail got worse. Might be microbatch sizing change? :thinking_face:
Devon P: I suspect the new GEMM kernel is slightly slower at small sequence lengths. We optimized for long sequences; short-seq kernel fallback could be failing.
Sam K: Good call. We swapped kernel selector logic in the rollout that favors the new fused-kernel for most layers. If it loses on short sequences, that could impact streaming perceived latency even if total tokens/sec is okay.
Tess R: Can we confirm with profiler traces? I have some traces for a 1-token stream workload.
Devon P: Pasted a trimmed perf sample from prod (aggregated):
```
# sample summary (short seq workloads)
kernel_fused_attention: 42% (median)
kernel_small_gemm: 55% (median)
context_switch/overhead: 3%
avg_token_latency_ms: 18
p95_token_latency_ms: 72 (was 42 before selector change)
```
Looks like fused attention emits slightly higher p95 for 1/2 token chunks.
Yara M: Also noticed KV cache hits are behaving oddly with batching. When microbatch size >1, KV cache reuse seems lower because requests are routed to different workers (sticky routing changed in rollout). That may be adding recompute.
Sam K: Oof. So two potential causes: kernel choice for short seqs and routing affecting KV cache hit rate. Both increase tail. We need to split experiments to isolate.
Tess R: Proposed AB test: revert kernel selector to previous heuristic on 10% of traffic and enable sticky routing for small prompt-size buckets for another 10%. Measure p50/p95/p99 for first-byte and overall completion.
Devon P: Agree. Also we should test microbatch sizing: microbatch=1 vs 4 vs 8 for streaming workloads. Streaming perceived latency often benefits from smaller microbatches even if throughput drops.
Sam K: Can you enumerate the metric set we'll track? I want to correlate kernel-level timings with network flush intervals and chunk size.
Devon P: Metrics: stream_first_byte_latency (p50/p95/p99), chunk_flush_interval_ms, average microbatch_size, KV_cache_hit_rate, kernel_selector_decision_counts, tokens_per_sec. Also tail-queued-time from runtime queue.
Yara M: Don't forget user-perceived metric: time_to_first_non-empty_chunk. With chunk_size too large or flush interval high, perceived latency spikes even if server generates tokens quickly.
Tess R: On flush intervals — current default is 40ms for 8-token chunks in the streaming layer. We experimented with 20ms/40ms/80ms. 20ms gave best perceived latency but higher network overhead. 80ms reduced throughput ops but the p95 perceived latency jumped.
Sam K: We need a cost-latency curve per workload. For low prompt length workloads (LL) prefer microbatch=1, kernel=small_gemm, flush=20ms; for long generation (LG) prefer microbatch>4, fused kernels, flush=40-80ms. Can we encode policies?
Devon P: Yes — we already have policy routing by request-size; just need to refine heuristics: sequence_length_estimate -> preferred_kernel, preferred_microbatch, flush_interval. We'll add fallback when KV_cache_hit_rate drops below 60%.
Yara M: Quick question on profiling: how do we tag kernel decisions in traces? I saw a milestone tag earlier but it's not in flamegraphs.
Devon P: We emit kernel_selector tag on the request trace and per-layer kernel id in the runtime perf event stream. The ingest pipeline needs to join those events. I'm adding a small patch to include kernel id as span attribute so it's visible in traces.
Tess R: For the experiment, I'll roll out three variants: (A) revert kernel selector + sticky routing, (B) current selector + sticky routing, (C) current selector + sticky routing + smaller flush (20ms) for short-seq bucket. 10% traffic each. Measure one week.
Sam K: Sounds good. If we see improvement in p95 for A and C, we can consider hybrid selector: prefer small kernel for seq<8 and fused otherwise; ensure sticky routing for short buckets to maintain KV cache locality.
Yara M: Side note: we observed a perf regression in an unrelated commit that increased context_switch/overhead for CUDA streams by 1.5ms on average. Might be due to additional synchronization in the allocator. That could also amplify tail effects when combined with the kernel change.
Devon P: I'll bisect the allocator change and add a microbenchmark focusing on stream synchronization latency. If allocator sync adds >1ms per token under high concurrency, it's unacceptable for low-latency tier.
Tess R: Logging/alerts: create an alert that triggers if stream_first_byte_p95 increases by >15ms vs baseline for >10min, and another for KV_cache_hit_rate drop >20% for short-seq bucket.
Sam K: Great. Action items:
- Devon: patch traces to include kernel id span, run allocator bisect microbench (ETA 24h).
- Tess: configure AB variants, adjust routing policy for short-seq buckets, create alerts (ETA 48h).
- Yara: pull historical KV cache hit rates by routing version and correlate with p95 (ETA 24h).
- Sam: run cost-latency curves for candidate flush intervals and microbatch sizes and share spreadsheet (ETA 48h).
infra-bot: Deployed experiment config to staging for variants A/B/C. Logs: experiment-1746001234 staged.
Devon P: I'll start with a small microbenchmark: single-token streaming on T4 vs A100, compare kernel_fused vs kernel_small_gemm, microbatch 1/4/8, flush 20/40/80ms. Post results here.
Yara M: Thanks. If anyone needs synthetic load scripts for short-seq streaming, ping me. I've got a small harness that mimics PLG chat traffic.
Sam K: Thanks team. Let's reconvene after the first round of telemetry (48-72h). :thumbsup:
